component.name: OpenExtract
component.summary: Get your texts off an iPhone backup and search them

description.p: Getting your text messages off an iPhone is harder than it should be. OpenExtract opens an iPhone backup on your own computer and lets you read, search and save everything in it: messages and iMessages, WhatsApp chats, photos, voicemails, contacts, call history, notes and podcasts.
It is free with no strings attached. There is no account, no trial and no paid tier, and nothing you open is ever uploaded. This Flatpak has no network access at all.

ul.li: Read whole conversations as chat bubbles, with photos
Read WhatsApp chats and groups, with replies, reactions, photos and voice messages
Search inside a conversation, and find conversations by name
Save a conversation as a PDF, with its photos
Export conversations as HTML, CSV or plain text
Save voicemails as audio files and photos as ordinary image files
See the podcasts you follow and the episodes you played, and save your subscriptions for another podcast app
Opens encrypted backups with the backup password

screenshot.caption: Everything in the backup on one page
One search box for messages, notes, calls and more
Voicemails you can play and save

description.p: A backup deleted from the computer no longer stays in Your backups, and on Mac and Windows each backup there now has a ⋯ menu to show it in Finder or File Explorer, move it to the Trash or Recycle Bin, or take it off the list. Back up my iPhone warns when the chosen folder is in OneDrive, iCloud Drive, Dropbox or Google Drive. Saving photos from an encrypted backup no longer needs the whole library's size free on this computer's own drive, a photo that can't be shown now says so, and attachments saved with a Messages webpage keep their message's date.

Saving now asks, once each time you open OpenExtract, what it's worth to you: $5, $25, $100 or any amount, with Save without paying right beside it. Calls no longer shows changes to a group chat (someone added or removed, a new name) as FaceTime calls, and Messages now says "Attachment not in this backup", instead of "Conversation update", when the iPhone removed a photo or file from a message.

Notes now shows every note in the backup. An iPhone that has kept notes since before iOS 9 could show only a few old ones and hide the rest, and a note that's only numbers showed a blank page. A note still in the iPhone's Recently Deleted folder is now marked that way, and the Timeline, Year view and whole-backup search leave it out. Choosing a folder to open a backup from no longer lists the same backup several times, finds backups beside thousands of other folders or in two-letter folders like "de", and on a Mac no longer stops to ask for access to other apps' data.

On Photos you can now pick the photos you want and save just those, narrow the grid to the days they were taken, and see just the photos of the people you pick, from the groups of faces your iPhone's Photos app found. Saving photos into a folder you've used before says how many were already there, and the grid fills much faster. Each PDF of a conversation now holds about half as many photos and pages, so a computer short on memory can print it. Choosing a folder above a backup, such as MobileSync or a drive, now finds the backups inside it, and when a folder has no backup the app says what it does hold. Someone who saves from a sixth different iPhone in a year is asked once whether it's paid work; nothing in the app changes either way.

Two new sections: Voice Memos, with the iPhone's recordings, their transcripts and Recently Deleted, and Calendar, with every event and calendar files (.ics) to save. On People, photos, videos, voice messages and documents now show on each message as they do on the phone, and Save everything saves your whole history with someone, with every file. A chat too big for one PDF is saved as one PDF per year. Back up my iPhone no longer ruins the backup already in a folder when a new backup fails partway: if one failed with 0.18.0 or earlier, see Fixed below. Older backups can be moved to the Trash from Backup details. Saves never replace a file that's already there, so photos that share a name like IMG_0001 are all saved, and a save that runs out of room says so instead of calling photos "not in this backup". Long saves from encrypted backups are much faster and show how far they've got.

Voicemail transcripts now show, under each voicemail and in search. Back up my iPhone no longer hangs for up to 5 minutes when a connected iPhone doesn't answer, and on Windows a backup the iPhone has finished no longer fails at the very last step. Videos in a backup that isn't encrypted open in your video player. Saved call history, web history, notes and voicemail lists show times in your own time zone instead of UTC, a backup whose folder is missing files now says so, and when WhatsApp's chats aren't in a backup, the app says why. New and experimental: Export a data bundle saves messages, calls, voicemail, contacts and photo details in one documented folder that other tools can read.

Voicemail now has Spam and Deleted lists beside Voicemail, as on the iPhone. Spam voicemails used to be mixed in with the rest, deleted ones still in the backup weren't shown at all, and some older deleted ones showed up as if they hadn't been deleted. Save all saves every list, and a voicemail whose recording isn't in the backup now says so instead of failing to play.

OpenExtract stays free for everyone, no strings. After an export, a Pay it forward note from Charles asks you to pay what it's worth to you, but only if you can. It has a Pay $5 button, and if you can't, Say thanks lets you send a thank-you note instead. Photos now lists Favorites, Hidden and the album folders you made on the phone. As on the iPhone, All Photos and Favorites leave out photos you've hidden: they're under Hidden. Save to this computer still saves every photo and video, hidden ones included. Back up my iPhone no longer asks for a new password when the iPhone already has a backup password.
Backing up an iPhone works again. In 0.15.0 every backup stopped at once saying pymobiledevice3 is not installed, because part of the code that talks to iPhones was left out when the app was built.

Podcasts has its own section: the shows you follow in Apple Podcasts and the episodes you played, newest first, with how many times and where you stopped. Save your subscriptions as an OPML file, which most podcast apps can import, or every show and episode as a spreadsheet. A backup never includes podcast audio, so each episode has a Get audio button that opens it in your browser. When a recent backup has moved or its drive isn't plugged in, the app says so and offers Find it. Saving inside OpenExtract's own program folder is refused, because an update would delete it.

WhatsApp has its own section: chats, groups and broadcast lists in the order they arrived, with replies, reactions, calls, locations, photos, videos, voice messages and documents. Save a chat, or all of them, as a web page, PDF, CSV or text file. WhatsApp messages also show in the Timeline, in search and under each person in People. If WhatsApp's end-to-end encrypted backup is turned on, WhatsApp leaves its chats out of the iPhone's backup, so there's nothing to show. The Timeline no longer shows a calls error on backups that aren't encrypted.

Big backups no longer stop after 2 hours while they're still copying, and the computer stays awake while a backup runs. A backup that stopped partway is marked "Didn't finish" instead of opening as if it were complete, and backups made by iOS 6 open without stopping OpenExtract. When a backup can't go on, the message says why: a full drive, another app syncing the iPhone, the passcode, or the connection dropping.

The first screen now lists the iPhone backups already on this computer, each with an Open button, so most people don't need to pick a folder. Encrypted backups of iPhones on iOS 10.0 or 10.1 open with their password. "Not now" on the update card no longer turns update checks off for good: the card comes back a week later.

Conversations saved as a web page now include their photos, GIFs, videos and other files, in a folder beside the page. Backups made by iOS 9 and earlier, the ones with a Manifest.mbdb file, open now, encrypted ones too. Saved conversations get readable file names and show times in your time zone, and notices in a conversation say what happened, such as who was added or who left. Saved photos keep the date they were taken, and saving a big photo library shows how far it has got instead of timing out. OpenExtract also starts faster, because its engine no longer unpacks itself each time.

A new look that's simpler to find your way around: a backup opens on a home page with a tile for each kind of data, and from there you can search the whole backup, with results grouped by kind. People shows everyone you were in touch with, each on one page, and Year view shows the backup as a heatmap with one square per day. Clicking a photo now opens it full size, and Settings says that Flathub keeps the app up to date.

Send feedback or report a problem from inside the app: the report is filled in with the app and phone details, with personal details left out, and opens in your browser for you to check and send. The app also says right away when its engine stops, instead of waiting with no message.

Calls from other apps show readable names, numbers saved in a local format match international ones, and older call history formats load. Text fields no longer download spell-check dictionaries, and the app has its own icon.
Save a conversation as a PDF, with its photos. Photo counts now cover only the photos in the backup, and exports say what a message without text is.
